themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 20 THIS WEEK, a 186% increase from the 7.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.51), suggesting rapid deterioration of street-level vegetation management across St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: 20 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average (186% spike, z-score 7.51)
Corresponds with 22 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK (135% above 9.4 average), suggesting infrastructure decay may be connected
Spike is statistically severe (z-score 7.51 indicates rare event outside normal variation)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about maintenance schedules and staffing gaps in CD 501
Document safety hazards from overgrown branches (blocked sightlines, pedestrian obstruction) with photos/video

themes_detail.label: Standing Water Emergence
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints exploded to 3 LAST WEEK from a near-zero baseline of 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), indicating a possible drainage system failure or localized flooding event.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Water System complaints also spiked to 112 three weeks ago (166% above 42.1 average), suggesting broader water infrastructure stress
Temporal alignment suggests potential drainage or main water line issue
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP/HPD inspection records for the specific locations reporting standing water
Interview affected residents about duration, location, and health/property impacts

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 22 THIS WEEK, a 135% increase from the 9.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.65), potentially linked to seasonal freeze-thaw cycles or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 22 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.4 weekly average (135% spike, z-score 3.65)
Overlaps with overgrown tree/branch spike (20 complaints this week)—fallen branches may be damaging sidewalks
Long-standing community board budget request for street repairs suggests chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Map specific neighborhoods within CD 501 with highest complaint density
Interview DOT about repair backlogs and whether weather or tree damage is primary cause

themes_detail.label: Construction/Plumbing Spike (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 31 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 94% increase from the 16.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.8), suggesting either major renovation activity or systemic plumbing failures affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 31 construction/plumbing complaints two weeks ago vs. 16.0 weekly average (94% spike, z-score 4.8)
644 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (432 alterations, 125 new buildings) indicates active development pressure
Water System complaints (112 three weeks ago) and standing water spike suggest connected infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Cross-reference spike dates with major DOB permit approvals to identify common projects
Interview residents about noise/disruption from simultaneous construction projects

themes_detail.label: Litter/Waste Management Decline
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 8 LAST WEEK (300% above 2.0 average) and dumpster complaints hit 5 TWO WEEKS AGO (700% above 0.6 average), indicating deteriorating sanitation infrastructure or inadequate waste container placement.
evidence: 8 litter basket requests last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 4.54)
5 dumpster complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.41)
Missed collection complaints remain elevated at 665 complaints over 90 days, suggesting chronic sanitation staffing issues
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about staffing levels and collection schedules in CD 501
Document specific locations with missing/overflowing bins or dumpster problems
